title: Announced-starter evidence register - dated official announcements, never inferred replacements
requirement: Add an announced-starter evidence field: the blank replacement columns on the injury-report page are correct there, but the league DOES publish dated starter announcements; record them with their clock dates and links, separately from anything inferred.
rule: A row is published only when the announcement itself was read on an official page this session. Where the official document announces a roster event rather than a start, the announced_start column stays blank and the roster event is recorded as evidence - the distinction between 'announced to start' and 'likely to start' is preserved verbatim.

rows.announcement: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Lock has no injury designation and WILL START Sunday vs. the Raiders; the article adds Lock is filling in for the injured Sam Darnold and making his third start of the season.
rows.cross_check: data/injuries.tsv Week 10 capture: SEA Sam Darnold DNP/Out (Ribs, Quadricep) and Drew Lock LIMITED with no game status - consistent with an announced healthy starter.

rows.roster_event: Official: the Cardinals finalized a trade sending Brissett to the Ravens (announced Friday). The same official article states Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve and out indefinitely, Tyler Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury, and Baltimore had a different starting quarterback for a third consecutive game.
rows.cross_check: The article's own words about Week 10 are that Brissett 'presumably will start' - a reporter inference, NOT an announcement. The announced_start cell is therefore blank; publishing it as an announced start would be exactly the inference this register exists to prevent.

rows.roster_event: Official: the league's reserve-list transaction table shows Malik Willis (MIA) placed on Reserve/Injured on 11/10 (raw capture: raw/nfl-reserve-list-2026-11.md).
rows.cross_check: League-adjacent reporting says McCord made his first NFL start in Week 10, and data/injuries.tsv is consistent (MIA Tua Tagovailoa-era depth moves; Willis absent from the weekly report because he is on IR, not because he is healthy - the brief's exact 'not listed != available' case). No official page announcing the START itself was read this session, so the announced_start cell stays blank (flag F64).

rows.roster_event: Official article of 2026-11-06: Jackson 'is on injured reserve and out indefinitely'; Huntley 'suffered a turf toe injury that has ended his season'; Baltimore started a different QB for a third consecutive game (Joe Fagnano started vs. Jacksonville in Week 9).
rows.cross_check: This is the evidence behind the brief's stale-depth flag: any club depth page still publishing Jackson/Huntley as the QB line must be read against this dated event, never as a current starter statement.

open_items: McCord (AS-03): an official dated start announcement is still to be captured; the reserve transaction is captured.
The register currently covers Week 10 evidence only; it extends week by week as announcements are read from official pages.
Club depth-chart pages are NOT treated as start announcements anywhere in this register: a chart is an unofficial depth statement, not a dated starter declaration.
